title: Document with sections
description: One RIS decision as in document.schema.json, plus its coarse sections: the subsections of the reasoning, detected from the headings printed in the text, and a structure template per decision. Citations are a separate derived object.

ecli.description: ECLI as given by RIS. Never derived from the RIS ID (the suffixes can differ).

case_number.description: First case number (Geschaeftszahl) in the RIS metadata.

case_numbers.description: All case numbers the decision covers: the RIS metadata plus joined case numbers printed at the head of the decision. The first item equals case_number.

document_numbers.description: Case numbers with the document suffix as printed at the head of the decision (BVwG: 'L519 2309863-1/7E'). Distinguishes decisions that share a case number. Empty if the decision prints none.

decision_date.description: RIS Entscheidungsdatum. For orally pronounced decisions this is the date of the written copy.

pronouncement_date.description: Date of oral pronouncement ('mündlich verkündet') stated at the head of the decision, else null.

decision_type.description: RIS Entscheidungsart normalised: Erkenntnis -> judgment, Beschluss -> order. The raw value stays in ris_metadata.

ris_metadata.description: The RIS OGD API record Data.Metadaten, verbatim.

full_text.description:
Deterministic text of the decision, built from the RIS XML (not the HTML). (1) Units: one paragraph per RIS paragraph element (), list item (: its symbol, a space, the text) and list closing paragraph (, ), and one per table row (see paragraph). (2) Left out: page headers and footers, the RIS header fields (Gericht, Entscheidungsdatum, Geschäftszahl, ECLI), the RIS field labels, the editorial VfGH Leitsatz (kept in ris_metadata) and images. (3) Inline elements: -> '-'; ,
, , -> space; , , -> '&', '<', '>'. (4) Characters: U+00A0 -> space; U+00AD removed; Word symbol-font bullets U+F0B7 and U+F095 -> '•', U+F02D -> '-'; every other character unchanged. (5) Whitespace runs -> one space; each paragraph trimmed. (6) Paragraphs joined by a single '\n'. (7) Footnotes (/): one paragraph per footnote, after all other paragraphs, in a section of type other with source_label 'Fußnoten'; the reference marks carry no text.

structure.description: How the reasoning is divided by the heading rules (config/segmentation/bvwg_headings.yaml) and the hierarchy rules (src/asylum_corpus/segmentation/subsections.py). status: the structure template the recognised headings form, tested in this order: abridged, no_reasoning, none, merits, merits_incomplete, short, ab_only. merits (findings, assessment of evidence and legal assessment, in this order), merits_incomplete (one or two of them, or all three out of order), short (no findings / evidence / legal assessment, but procedural history and/or 'erwogen'), ab_only (only 'Zu A)' / 'Zu B)'), none (a reasoning without any recognised heading), abridged (an abridged written decision, gekürzte Ausfertigung: a reasoning of at most 3,000 characters with the standard note of § 29 Abs. 5 VwGVG), no_reasoning (no reasoning section, one shorter than 500 characters, or one that only repeats head and operative part). Combined headings count as both their parts; procedural_history_and_findings counts as findings only where the decision has an assessment of evidence or legal assessment section. The template describes the document as printed, not the kind of decision.

hierarchy_rules_applied.description: The hierarchy rules that changed the result for this document, in alphabetical order (src/asylum_corpus/segmentation/subsections.py; parents and extent always apply, fallback and erwogen_as_legal are not listed): zu_a_before_history 'Zu A)' before the procedural history dropped; inside_history headings before an 'erwogen' heading (from the start of the reasoning or a procedural history heading) dropped; own_part_in_history a heading with the label of the first procedural history heading kept as the court's own part; erwogen_after_legal an 'erwogen' heading right after a legal assessment heading dropped (its opening sentence); subtitle a heading right after a heading of the same type dropped (its subtitle); sub_point a repeated type with a deeper label dropped as a sub-point; zu_a_encloses 'Zu A)' enclosing findings / evidence / legal assessment; point_of_evidence a findings heading inside the assessment of evidence dropped (its point); out_of_order findings / evidence / legal assessment out of order.

offset.description: Character offset into full_text (start inclusive, end exclusive).

section.description: A contiguous run of paragraphs. Level 1: the sections from the RIS fields, with the type and span they have in document.schema.json (they partition full_text; types may repeat); all IDs are numbered anew in document order. Level 2 and deeper: subsections of a reasoning section, each starting with its heading paragraph and ending before the next heading of the same or a higher level (or at the end of its parent). Sections are listed in document order (by start, then level).

type.description: Level 1 (RIS fields): subject, operative_part, reasoning, other - as in document.schema.json. Subsections of the reasoning (from printed headings): procedural_history (Verfahrensgang); procedural_history_and_findings (a procedural history heading that names the facts too, 'Verfahrensgang und Sachverhalt'; counts as findings for the templates only where the decision has an assessment of evidence or legal assessment section); considerations ('Das Bundesverwaltungsgericht hat erwogen'); findings (Feststellungen, Sachverhalt); evidence_assessment (Beweiswürdigung, or where there is no such heading the sentence that opens it); legal_assessment (Rechtliche Beurteilung; in a decision without such a heading, also an 'erwogen' heading that follows the court's findings or assessment of evidence and is followed by neither); findings_and_evidence ('Feststellungen und Beweiswürdigung'); legal_and_evidence ('Rechtliche Beurteilung und Beweiswürdigung'); ruling_a ('Zu A)': the reasoning on operative part A); revision_admissibility ('Zu B)': whether an appeal to the VwGH is admissible).

source_label.description: The label of the RIS field the section comes from (Betreff, Spruch, Begründung, Text, ...), else its field code; 'Fußnoten' for the footnotes.

parent_id.description: The enclosing section; null for level 1.

level.description: 1 for the RIS-field sections; a subsection's level is its parent's plus one (deepest: reasoning 1 > considerations 2 > 'Zu A)' enclosing the merits 3 > legal assessment 4 > 'Zu A)' 5).

detection.description: xml_field: from the RIS field (level 1). heading_rule: from a heading printed in the text, recognised by a rule of config/segmentation/bvwg_headings.yaml.

rule.description: ID of the heading rule; null for xml_field sections.

heading_paragraph_id.description: The paragraph holding the heading (the first paragraph of the subsection); null for xml_field sections.

decision_form.description: operative_part sections: the form of this part of the decision as its introductory sentence states it ('zu Recht erkannt:', 'zu Recht:', 'erkannt:' -> judgment; 'beschlossen:', 'den Beschluss gefasst:' -> order; 'zu Recht erkannt und beschlossen:' -> judgment_and_order); null without such a sentence and for all other sections. Recorded as printed: the document's decision_type stays as RIS states it. The two differ in about 0.8 % of the documents, with errors on both sides; the legally correct form is an interpretation and belongs to the outcome annotation.

paragraph.description: One RIS paragraph element (<absatz>), list item (<listelem>) or list closing paragraph (<schluss>, <schlussteil>) whose text is not empty after normalisation (see full_text). A leading structural margin number is moved to marginal_number. Tables: one paragraph per row; each cell's paragraph elements are joined by a space, the cells are joined in column order by ' | ', empty cells are kept so the columns stay aligned, and rows whose cells are all empty are dropped; a table nested in a cell is part of that cell's text (only the rows of the outer table are paragraphs). full_text[start:end] == text.

section_id.description: The deepest section containing the paragraph.

marginal_number.description: Margin number (Randzahl) that the RIS XML marks structurally (a number followed by a tab at the start of the paragraph, used by the VwGH); removed from text. Outline labels such as '1.1.', 'II.' or 'a)' stay in the text.
